dictations.preRound: Day 3 of IV cefazolin for the left lower leg cellulitis. Redness is receding inside the marked border. Afebrile overnight, Tmax 37.4. He is on a statin at home and we are continuing it. BP 124/78, heart rate 82. WBC 9.8, down from 13.1.
dictations.encounter: Leg is less warm and less tender, redness now about 2 cm inside the line. Walking in the hall. Plan to switch to oral cephalexin tomorrow if the redness keeps improving. Consider a CT of the leg only if it stops improving.

note:
Subjective

Not provided

Objective

Vital Signs: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 82 bpm, temperature 37.4°C.

Physical Examination: Leg is less warm and less tender, redness now approximately 2 cm inside the marked line. Patient ambulating in the hall.

Testing Results

White blood cell count 9.8 (down from 13.1 on admission).

Assessment

Patient is a 67-year-old male with no past medical history documented in the available records who presented with left lower leg cellulitis. He is now on day 3 of intravenous cefazolin with receding erythema, afebrile, and improving leukocytosis. The clinical picture is consistent with resolving cellulitis with good response to antibiotic therapy. Plan is to transition to oral therapy as the infection continues to improve.

Plan

1. Left lower leg cellulitis — continue intravenous cefazolin; plan to switch to oral cephalexin tomorrow if redness continues to improve; consider computed tomography of the leg only if redness stops improving.

2. Continue home statin (dose not specified in dictation).
